programmes.name: Cyber Security

sources.title: Cyber Security is an English-taught 195 ECTS bachelor in Viborg beginning September 2027, with a six-month internship and an optional two-year AP exit.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: Facts list English, Viborg, September 2027, 195 ECTS, 3¼ years and a six-month internship. The first 1½ years are shared; applicants apply to the bachelor and may exit after two years with an Academy Profession Degree in Operational Cyber Security. Semesters 1–3 cover business understanding, programming, computer architecture, communication, automation, data and network security, governance and software security. Semester 6 is a 30 ECTS internship; semester 7 includes a 10 ECTS bachelor project. Semester 4 Governance, Risk & Compliance is pending approval; specialisation and certification detail is due in November.

sources.title: The Danish counterpart names the professional bachelor award and explicitly opens applications on 1 February 2027.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: The Danish page names Professionsbachelor i Cybersikkerhed, 195 ECTS and 3¼ years, and states applications open 1 February 2027 for September 2027 start. It labels its own teaching language Danish; the separately linked English programme page explicitly labels its international offering English.

sources.title: Dania describes small classes, industry contact and international-student and housing guidance at its Viborg campus.

notes: Governance, Risk & Compliance is pending approval. Specialisation and certification details are due in November; confirm the final curriculum before applying.
programmes.description: The first year covers business understanding, programming, computer architecture, communication, automation, data security and network architecture. The second year adds cybersecurity governance, network and communication security, software security and system security. Later study includes specialisation or an international semester, internship, certification and a bachelor project. Governance, Risk & Compliance remains pending approval; Dania promises further specialisation and certification details in November.

structure.teachingStyle: Smaller classes, classroom teaching and group work, with occasional lectures and company visits.
structure.placement: Six-month internship in semester 6, worth 30 ECTS.
structure.studyAbroad: Semester 5 is listed as specialisation or an international semester; detailed choices have not yet been announced.
structure.flexibility: Apply to the bachelor; the first 1½ years are shared with the optional two-year AP exit in Operational Cyber Security. The full bachelor lasts 3¼ years.
specialisations: Details to be announced; no confirmed specialisation choices yet.

programmes.about: Study programming, data and network security, and security governance in Viborg. This English professional bachelor starts in September 2027 and includes a six-month internship; you may instead exit after two years with an AP degree in Operational Cyber Security.

language.note: The English programme page explicitly confirms English and September 2027; the Danish counterpart describes a Danish-language offering.

admission.capacityNote: The Danish counterpart states limited intake; a numerical 2027 capacity is not published.

selection.description: Quota 2 considers additional qualifications alongside entry requirements. Dania does not publish a weighting or scoring rubric.

sources.title: Cyber Security requires English B and Mathematics B; quota 2 considers additional qualifications.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: Specific entry requirements state English at Danish B level (210 hours of 60 minutes over the last three upper-secondary years) and mathematics at Danish B level (250 hours). Applicants applying by 15 March noon are assessed in quota 2, including additional qualifications. No weighting or complete scoring rubric is given.

requirements.label: IB Diploma, or Course Results: 18+ points, six subjects at grade 3+, including at least three HL subjects

officialWording.text: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2.

requirements.note: National recognition rules give these Course Results general access to professional bachelor programmes through quotas 1 and 2. The English B and Mathematics B subject requirements still apply. Dania must assess the submitted qualification and subject evidence.

sources.title: A full IB Diploma qualifies for general access; qualifying Course Results give access to Danish AP and professional bachelor programmes, including this programme type.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: An IB Diploma of at least 24 points gives general access subject to specific requirements. Course Results of at least 18 points, with grade 3 or better in all six subjects and at least three HL subjects, give access through quotas 1 and 2 to academy-profession and professional bachelor programmes. The university-bachelor supplementation rule is separate and does not apply to this professional bachelor.

sources.title: Dania lists English tests with two-year validity but its English C plus test wording conflicts with the programme-specific English B requirement.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: Under English requirements the page says English C plus an English test can satisfy the language requirement. Minimum scores listed are IELTS Academic or Indicator 6.5; TOEFL or TOEFL iBT Home Edition 4.5 or 94; Cambridge C1 Advanced 180; Cambridge C2 Proficiency 200; Oxford Online Placement Test C1 with at least 85 in each part, accepted only at Dania or an approved partner agency. sources.quote: Structured restatement: Apply through optagelse.dk from 1 February; the deadline for non-Danish upper-secondary qualifications is 15 March at noon. Upload diploma and transcript; if graduating after the deadline, upload the latest transcript by the application deadline and the final diploma as soon as received, following admission-period instructions. Translation is not required. Upload a signed and stamped upper-secondary verification form and photo ID. The exact September 2027 start date is not yet announced; orientation is in the preceding week.
